messages.content:
Rewrite as just two sentences.

In a busy Madrid supermarket, Mateo, almost three, dropped flat onto the cold floor by the fruit. He screamed, kicked his shoes off and arched his back like a bridge. His dad, Sami, crouched down. "Mateo, listen, we'll..." Mateo threw a mandarin, then another. He couldn't hear a word. His cheeks were scarlet and his breath came in gulps. Sami moved the bag of apples out of reach and waited.

In a busy Madrid supermarket, Mateo, almost three, threw himself on the floor, screaming, kicking and throwing mandarins, too upset to hear a word. His dad, Sami, crouched beside him, moved the apples out of reach and waited.
Turn this paragraph into numbered steps: To make chai, boil water with tea leaves, then add milk and sugar, let it simmer for two minutes, and strain it into cups.

1. Boil water with tea leaves.
2. Add milk and sugar.
3. Let it simmer for two minutes.
4. Strain the chai into cups.

Make this shorter, under 60 words.

I'm Chandrika, and I sit next to Bhavna in Class 6. Yesterday a classmate brought a shiny new geometry box with a magnetic lid and twelve coloured pens. Bhavna kept glancing at it all through maths. She opened and closed her own old tin box, the one with a dent. At lunch, she asked the girl, 'Where did you buy it?' and then, 'How much?' When she heard the answer she went quiet. I'm not sure what she was thinking, but she held her dented box on her lap for a long time.

I'm Chandrika, and I sit next to Bhavna in Class 6. Yesterday a classmate brought a shiny geometry box with a magnetic lid and twelve coloured pens. Bhavna kept glancing at it, asked where it was bought and how much it cost, then went quiet and held her dented tin box on her lap for a long time.
Make this get-well note warmer: Get well soon. Rest and come back.
Get well soon! We're thinking of you. Take all the rest you need, and we'll be so happy to see you back.
Can you change to the past tense: The potter shapes the clay, the wheel spins fast, and the pot slowly rises.
The potter shaped the clay, the wheel spun fast, and the pot slowly rose.

Use easier words and shorter sentences for this passage.

Monday: Tejas teased his sister Diya about her missing front tooth until she squealed. Wednesday: At the park, Hrithik from the next lane shoved Diya off the swing, and she landed on her hands. Tejas dropped his bat and ran. He stood in front of her and said, "Don't touch my sister." His voice shook, but his fists stayed open. He took Diya's hand, walked her home and told Papa what happened. Friday: Tejas was calling Diya "gap-tooth" again, but he gave her the bigger half of his biscuit while he did it.

On Monday, Tejas teased his sister Diya about her missing front tooth until she squealed. On Wednesday, Hrithik from the next lane pushed Diya off the swing at the park. She landed on her hands. Tejas dropped his bat and ran. He stood in front of her and said, "Don't touch my sister." His voice shook, but his fists stayed open. He took Diya's hand and walked her home. He told Papa what happened. On Friday, Tejas was calling Diya "gap-tooth" again. But he gave her the bigger half of his biscuit while he did it.

Simplify this for a young reader.

On the charpai outside, Salma, two, held her mother Aparna's phone, face lit by fast cartoons. She didn't hear the goats or her cousins.

When Aparna took the phone, Salma screamed and kicked.

Aparna stayed calm. "Come, let's feed the goat." She carried her to the pen.

Salma sniffled, then giggled as the goat nibbled grass from her hand.

Salma, two, sat on the charpai outside with her mother Aparna's phone. Fast cartoons lit up her face. She did not hear the goats or her cousins.

Aparna took the phone. Salma screamed and kicked.

Aparna stayed calm. "Come, let's feed the goat." She carried her to the pen.

Salma sniffled. Then she giggled as the goat nibbled grass from her hand.

Rewrite the conversation as reported speech, with no quotation marks.

"Why does Chintu get the mango kulfi and I get nothing?" Kamal muttered.
"Because his throat is sore and the doctor said cold things soothe it," said his mother, Rukmini, sitting down next to him.
"You have been quiet all week."
"Everybody asks about Chintu. Nobody asks about me." Then, quickly, "I feel bad saying that."
"You can feel both, Kamal."
"Can we go for a walk, just us, on Saturday?"
"Yes. And you can help me carry his soup tray, if you like."
Kamal nodded. "I do want him better."

Kamal muttered, asking why Chintu got the mango kulfi and he got nothing. His mother, Rukmini, sat down next to him and explained that Chintu's throat was sore and the doctor had said cold things soothe it. She added that Kamal had been quiet all week. Kamal said that everybody asked about Chintu and nobody asked about him, and then quickly said that he felt bad saying that. His mother told him that he could feel both. He asked if they could go for a walk, just the two of them, on Saturday. She said yes, and that he could help her carry Chintu's soup tray if he liked. Kamal nodded and said that he did want Chintu better.

Put what people say here into reported speech.

Dolma had been sick with a cough and fever for three days. She was proud of drinking from a big-girl cup, but now she asked for her old baby bottle from the cupboard. She talked in a squeaky baby voice and crawled into Preeti's bed every night. Her aunt laughed, 'Such a big girl, acting like a baby!' Dolma hid her face. Preeti said gently, 'She's poorly. It's fine,' and filled the bottle with warm water. A week later, fever gone, Dolma pushed the bottle away herself. 'That's for babies.'

Dolma had been sick with a cough and fever for three days. She was proud of drinking from a big-girl cup, but now she asked for her old baby bottle from the cupboard. She talked in a squeaky baby voice and crawled into Preeti's bed every night. Her aunt laughed and said that she was such a big girl, acting like a baby. Dolma hid her face. Preeti said gently that Dolma was poorly and that it was fine, and filled the bottle with warm water. A week later, with the fever gone, Dolma pushed the bottle away herself and said that it was for babies.
Change from passive to active: A song was sung by the whole class at the farewell.
The whole class sang a song at the farewell.

Make this shorter, in two sentences.

Monday. Naveen crossed his eyes and puffed his cheeks. Simran giggled so hard she hiccupped.
Wednesday, at the clinic waiting room, another father tried the same face at her. Simran stared, frowned, and pressed her face into Naveen's side.
Friday evening. Naveen did the face again at home. Simran burst out laughing, then scrunched her own eyes and puffed her cheeks right back at him.

On Monday, Naveen crossed his eyes and puffed his cheeks and Simran giggled so hard she hiccupped, but on Wednesday she stared, frowned and hid her face against him when another father tried the same face at the clinic. On Friday evening Naveen did it again at home, and Simran burst out laughing and made the same face back.
Turn this casual message into a polite one for a shop owner: Hey, is my order ready yet?
Hello, could you please tell me whether my order is ready yet?
Change the speaker from "he" to "I": He forgot his umbrella, so he got wet.
I forgot my umbrella, so I got wet.
Swap "nice" for a stronger word: We had a nice dinner.
We had a lovely dinner.
Report these words without quotation marks: Arjun said, "I am hungry." His mother said, "Lunch is ready." He said, "Thank you."
Arjun said that he was hungry. His mother said that lunch was ready, and he thanked her.

Can you condense this to under 60 words?

My sister Kavitha had a science fair coming up, and I watched her spend Saturday morning on the floor of our room with a notebook. She wrote question after question. I read some upside down: "Why does ice float? Do plants like light? Can a spider smell?" She had ten. Then she started crossing them out. I don't know what she was thinking, but she kept looking around the room, at the window, at the cupboard, at Amma's plant pots on the balcony. By lunch she had only one left: "Do plants lean towards light?" She went to Amma and asked for two small pots. Our neighbour Naveen uncle gave her some bean seeds. By evening the pots were ready.

My sister Kavitha spent Saturday morning in our room writing ten science fair questions in a notebook. She crossed out all but one: "Do plants lean towards light?" She asked Amma for two small pots, and our neighbour Naveen uncle gave her some bean seeds. By evening the pots were ready.

Trim this email line down:

I am writing this message to let you know that I will not be able to attend tomorrow's meeting because I have another appointment at the same time.
I cannot attend tomorrow's meeting because I have another appointment at the same time.

Boil this down to a single sentence.

But by the first term's Physics test the picture looked different. Ojas stared at a page of forces and lenses that the other boys followed easily. His marks came in low.
By the first term's Physics test, Ojas was staring at a page of forces and lenses that the other boys followed easily, and his marks came in low.
Turn into the passive voice: The company opened a new office in Pune last year.
A new office was opened in Pune by the company last year.
Rewrite in the present tense: Ishaan kicked the ball, ran to the goal and shouted with joy.
Ishaan kicks the ball, runs to the goal and shouts with joy.
